Aus, bei, mit: sempre dativo, passo a pa: Aus, bei, mit: always dative, step by step
PASSO 1: sete preposições pedem SEMPRE o: STEP 1: seven prepositions ALWAYS take the dative: aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu. Learn them as a chant — German students sing them to "The Blue Danube": «aus-bei-mit-nach-seit-von-zu». STEP 2: «aus» = out of, from (origin) or made of: «Ich komme aus Brasilien» (I'm from Brazil), «aus dem Haus» (out of the house), «aus Holz» (made of wood). STEP 3: «bei» = at someone's place, at a business, near: «bei Anna» (at Anna's), «beim Arzt» (bei dem — at the doctor's), «bei der Arbeit» (at work). Note: «bei» is NOT "by" in the sense of "by bus". STEP 4: «mit» = with (company) and by (means of transport, tool): «mit meiner Mutter», «mit dem Zug» (by train), «mit dem Bus» (by bus). STEP 5: after these prepositions, the article is ALWAYS dative: dem (m), der (f), dem (n), den + -n (pl). STEP 6: contraction: bei dem = «beim».
o português usa «de», «em casa de», «com: English prepositions never change the noun after them ("with the bus", "from the house"). In German, the preposition decides the case: after aus, bei and mit, the article must turn dative (dem, der, den). And watch the false friends: «bei» ≠ "by", «mit dem Bus» = "by bus".

Nach, seit, von, zu: sempre dativo, pass: Nach, seit, von, zu: always dative, step by step
PASSO 1: «nach» tem dois usos: DEPOIS DE: STEP 1: «nach» has two uses: AFTER (time): «nach der Arbeit» (after work), «nach dem Essen» (after the meal); and TO with cities and countries (no article): «nach Berlin», «nach Brasilien». STEP 2: «seit» says how long something has been going on, and it uses the PRESENT tense — where English uses the present perfect: «Ich wohne seit zwei Jahren in Berlin» = I have lived in Berlin for two years. In the dative plural, the noun adds -n («Jahren»). STEP 3: «von» = from, of, by (origin, possession, author): «ein Brief von meiner Mutter» (a letter from my mother), «vom Chef» (von dem). STEP 4: «zu» = to people and places: «zum Arzt» (zu dem — to the doctor), «zur Schule» (zu der — to school), «zu meiner Oma» (to my grandma's). STEP 5: contractions: «zu dem» = «zum»; «zu der» = «zur»; «von dem» = «vom». STEP 6: «gegenüber» can come after the noun: «dem Bahnhof gegenüber» or «gegenüber dem Bahnhof» (across from the station).

PASSO 1: na fala e na escrita corrente,: STEP 1: in speech and everyday writing, the preposition and the article merge — like English "do not" → "don't": bei dem → beim; von dem → vom; zu dem → zum; zu der → zur. STEP 2: «mit dem» has no contraction (you always say «mit dem»). STEP 3: use the contracted form whenever the article is «dem» (masculine and neuter) or «der» (only with «zu»): «beim Arzt», «vom Bahnhof», «zum Supermarkt», «zur Schule».

— Sim, depois do trabalho gosto de ir a: — Yes, after work I like to walk.
